title: SEC6: pipeline detection before STARTTLS upgrade
description: In lifecycle.rs run_command_loop, the STARTTLS handler checks reader.buffer().is_empty() before sending the 382 response and returning to the caller for the TLS handshake. RFC 4642 forbids pipelining after STARTTLS; if the client has already queued commands in the TCP receive buffer, those bytes would be processed as TLS handshake bytes, enabling command injection or a STARTTLS stripping attack. The check correctly rejects the connection rather than silently tolerating pipelined data. Non-obvious because the buffer check must happen before the 382 is sent -- once 382 is flushed, the client begins TLS and any subsequently buffered bytes are the TLS ClientHello, not NNTP commands. Decision: close with 502 rather than ignore buffered data.
